Stance

/STANSS/ — rhymes with 'dance' · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Stance is a firmly held attitude or position on an issue.

The senator refused to soften her stance on clean-water protections.

Worked Example

At the town meeting, some neighbors wavered about the proposed skate park, changing their minds with each speaker. But Mr. Okafor stated clearly that he supported it, listed his reasons, and repeated the same position in every interview afterward.

Mr. Okafor took a stance — a settled attitude toward an issue that he held publicly. A passing 'opinion' can shift by dinnertime; a stance is a position you adopt, defend, and stand on.

How Stance Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

position

position: the side of an issue a person holds

viewpoint

viewpoint: a way of looking at an issue

attitude

attitude: a settled way of thinking or feeling about something

Antonyms

neutrality

neutrality: the state of taking no side

indecision

indecision: the inability to settle on a position

How Strong Is It? — leaning → stance → conviction

leaning vs. stance

leaning vs. stance: Leaning is weaker than stance — a leaning is only a slight tilt toward one side, while a stance is a position firmly taken and held.

conviction vs. stance

conviction vs. stance: Conviction is stronger than stance — a stance can be softened or revised, but a conviction is a belief held so deeply it defines you.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — sta-

root — sta-: to stand (Latin)

suffix — -nce

suffix — -nce: state or quality of (Latin via French)

Put it together

Put it together: From Latin stare, 'to stand.' Your stance is literally 'where you stand' — the position you take up and hold on an issue.
